# Review revenue recognition and deferred revenue

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When customer contracts create timing, allocation or uncertainty questions beyond collecting payment. A reviewed accounting policy and contract-level revenue schedule reconciled to the ledger and remaining performance obligations.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> Operational draft. Source checked on 2026-10-30. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance, certification or completed execution is claimed. The source context is IFRS; applicable accounting framework must be confirmed. Resolve applicable law and expert review before external action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Collect contracts and delivery evidence

agent-runnable


Gather signed agreements, amendments, invoices, credits and evidence of goods or services delivered. Identify bundled promises, variable fees and unusual acceptance terms for professional review.

- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Determine the applicable accounting framework

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The qualified accounting owner confirms the governing framework and contract treatment. This guide uses an IFRS overview as a reference and does not impose IFRS rules on entities using another framework.

- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the contract analysis and schedule

agent-runnable


Draft a contract-level schedule of promises, pricing assumptions, delivery dates and proposed recognition. Label judgments and distinguish cash collection, invoicing and recognized revenue.

- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review judgments and approve the accounting treatment

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The accounting owner reviews allocations, estimates, progress measures and contract changes under the applicable framework. Record support for judgments and escalate material uncertainty before posting.

- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Post approved entries through accounting controls

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized finance operators post the reviewed entries and retain approvals and source links. Reconcile recognized and deferred balances to the contract schedule and investigate differences.

- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Verify the close and refresh estimates

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The accounting owner reviews balances, remaining obligations and disclosure needs. Record changes in estimates and exceptions, with evidence for the next reporting close.

- Verify: A reviewed accounting policy and contract-level revenue schedule reconciled to the ledger and remaining performance obligations.
- Sources: [IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-15-revenue-from-contracts-with-customers/)
